claim: The subthalamic nucleus (STN) is a small almond-shaped subcortical structure classically known for its role in motor inhibition through the indirect pathway within the basal ganglia.
source: The subthalamic nucleus (STN) is a small almond-shaped subcortical structure classically known for its role in motor inhibition through the indirect pathway within the basal ganglia.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the STN's classical role in motor function.

claim: On high-uncertainty trials, STN spiking activity encodes the upcoming decision within a brief (500 ms) temporal window during the choice period, prior to the manifestation of the choice.
source: Intraoperative single-neuronal data from the STN reveals that on high-uncertainty trials, spiking activity encodes the upcoming decision within a brief (500 ms) temporal window during the choice period, prior to the manifestation of the choice.
evidence: This claim is supported by single-neuronal recordings presented in the study.

claim: Application of intermittent DBS selectively prior to the choice period alters decisions and biases subject behavior towards conservative wagers.
source: Application of intermittent DBS selectively prior to the choice period alters decisions and biases subject behavior towards conservative wagers.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from the intermittent stimulation study.

claim: Current DBS devices deliver continuous electrical stimulation to a targeted brain region to modify or reset aberrant neural activity or synchrony.
source: Current DBS devices deliver continuous electrical stimulation to a targeted brain region to modify or reset abberant neural activity or synchrony (Herrington et al., 2016a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The STN has a role in emotional processing.
source: More recently, a growing body of literature has begun to uncover a more nuanced role of the STN in higher-order cognitive processes such as, emotional processing (Le Jeune et al., 2009; Le Jeune et al., 2008; Drapier et al., 2006; Eitan et al., 2013), response inhibition (Frank et al., 2007; Cavanagh et al., 2011; Isoda and Hikosaka, 2008), and even psychiatric illness (Mallet et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The STN has a role in response inhibition.
source: More recently, a growing body of literature has begun to uncover a more nuanced role of the STN in higher-order cognitive processes such as, emotional processing (Le Jeune et al., 2009; Le Jeune et al., 2008; Drapier et al., 2006; Eitan et al., 2013), response inhibition (Frank et al., 2007; Cavanagh et al., 2011; Isoda and Hikosaka, 2008), and even psychiatric illness (Mallet et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The STN has a role in psychiatric illness.
source: More recently, a growing body of literature has begun to uncover a more nuanced role of the STN in higher-order cognitive processes such as, emotional processing (Le Jeune et al., 2009; Le Jeune et al., 2008; Drapier et al., 2006; Eitan et al., 2013), response inhibition (Frank et al., 2007; Cavanagh et al., 2011; Isoda and Hikosaka, 2008), and even psychiatric illness (Mallet et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The STN is an important deep brain stimulation (DBS) target for the treatment of movement disorders such as Parkinson's Disease (PD).
source: The STN is also an important deep brain stimulation (DBS) target for the treatment of movements disorders such as Parkinson's Disease (PD).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about DBS therapy.

claim: DBS surgery provides one of only a few opportunities to record neuronal responses in human subjects engaged in cognitive tasks.
source: DBS surgery provides one of only a few opportunities to record neuronal responses in humans subjects engaged in cognitive tasks (Zénon et al., 2016; Herz et al., 2016; Cavanagh et al., 2011; Zaghloul et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies that have used this approach.

claim: Studies of STN stimulation using current generation DBS systems have been limited by the systems' design to deliver continuous stimulation.
source: Studies of STN stimulation using current generation DBS systems have been limited by the systems' design to deliver continuous stimulation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the technical limitations of existing DBS systems.

claim: Targeting stimulation to specific temporal windows during the evolution of a cognitive process, rather than delivering long periods of continuous stimulation, will be critical to understanding the cognitive function and developing new neuromodulation therapies.
source: We hypothesized that targeting stimulation to specific temporal windows during the evolution of a cognitive process (e.g., decision-making), rather than delivering long periods of continuous stimulation, will be critical to understanding the cognitive function and developing new neuromodulation therapies going forward.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: This is the first study to apply intermittent DBS in humans actively engaged in a cognitive task.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to apply intermittent DBS in humans actively engaged in a cognitive task and the first to demonstrate a reduction in risk-seeking behavior following STN DBS.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: This is the first study to demonstrate a reduction in risk-seeking behavior following STN DBS.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to apply intermittent DBS in humans actively engaged in a cognitive task and the first to demonstrate a reduction in risk-seeking behavior following STN DBS.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: Subjects performed on average 1.83 sessions of the gambling task with an average of 105.2 trials per session.
source: On average subjects performed 1.83 sessions of the gambling task with an average of 105.2 trials per session.
evidence: This is descriptive data about the experimental sessions.

claim: All intraoperative subjects were off dopaminergic medications at least 12 hr prior to surgery.
source: In this study, all intraoperative subjects were off dopaminergic medications at least 12 hr prior to surgery.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol.

claim: The low-dopamine state may have contributed to subjects' risk-avoidant behavior.
source: The low-dopamine state may have contributed to subject's risk-avoidant behavior (St Onge et al., 2011; Claassen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation supported by citations to previous research.

claim: STN activity inhibits responses during cognitively demanding situations according to current models.
source: Current models suggest that STN activity inhibits responses during cognitively demanding situations (Frank, 2006; Frank et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to computational models.

claim: No other stimulus epoch correlated with subject behavior.
source: No other stimulus epoch correlated with subject behavior (Table 2).
evidence: This is a summary finding from the neural data analysis across different task epochs.

claim: The STN activity signal is unlikely to represent an overt finger movement because the task design balances the presentation of the $5 and $20 wagers equally to the left- and right-hand side of the screen.
source: This signal is unlikely to represent an overt finger movement because our task design balances the presentation of the $five and $20 wagers equally to the left- and right-hand side of the screen.
evidence: This is an inference based on the task design.

claim: All subjects in the intermittent stimulation study had completed surgery at least 6 months prior to the study.
source: All subjects had completed surgery at least 6 months prior tithe study.
evidence: This is a description of the inclusion criteria for the study.

claim: Subjects in the intermittent stimulation study performed on average 2 sessions of the gambling task with an average of 108 trials per session.
source: On average subjects performed 2 sessions of the gambling task with an average of 108 trials per session.
evidence: This is descriptive data about the experimental sessions.

claim: Subjects in the intermittent stimulation study were on their clinical regimen of dopamine replacement therapy during the experiment.
source: Unlike during the intraoperative sessions, subjects were on their clinical regimen of dopamine replacement therapy during this experiment.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol.

claim: 7 out of 11 subjects displayed a reduction in risk-seeking behavior with choice period stimulation.
source: We found that 7 out of 11 subjects displayed a reduction in risk-seeking behavior (Table 4).
evidence: This is a descriptive finding from the individual subject analysis.

claim: For the seven subjects that showed a reduction in risk-seeking behavior, the average magnitude of change was 12.8% (range: 1–18%).
source: Of the seven subjects the average magnitude of change was 12.8% (range: 1–18%).
evidence: This is a descriptive finding from the individual subject analysis.

claim: Three subjects showed an increase in risk-seeking behavior with an average magnitude of change of 12.1% (range: 2–22%).
source: For the three subjects that showed an increase in risk-seeking behavior, the average magnitude of change was 12.1% (range: 2–22%).
evidence: This is a descriptive finding from the individual subject analysis.

claim: One subject experienced no change in either direction from the stimulation.
source: One subject experienced no change in either direction from the stimulation.
evidence: This is a descriptive finding from the individual subject analysis.

claim: No similar differences in reaction times were observed for the omitted and fixation stimulation conditions.
source: No similar differences were observed for the omitted and fixation stimulation conditions.
evidence: This is a descriptive finding from the behavioral data analysis.

claim: Fleming et al. found a bilateral increase in BOLD response localized to the STN selectively for high-uncertainty trials where subjects responded against a status-quo bias.
source: In a recent functional imaging study, Fleming et al. found a bilateral increase in BOLD response localized to the STN selectively for high-uncertainty trials where subjects responded against a status-quo bias.
evidence: This is a citation to previous research findings.

claim: The same underlying mechanism observed by Fleming et al. may extend to value-based decisions made under conditions of uncertainty.
source: Although their study uses perceptual decisions, we demonstrate that the same underlying mechanism may extend to value-based decisions made under conditions of uncertainty.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of the current findings with previous work.

claim: Other studies have observed similar neural responses in the STN following conflict related encoding.
source: Other studies have observed similar neural responses in the STN following conflict related encoding (Cavanagh et al., 2011; Zaghloul et al., 2012) and control signal encoding (Isoda and Hikosaka, 2008; Wiecki and Frank, 2013).
evidence: This is a citation to previous research findings.

claim: Other studies have observed similar neural responses in the STN following control signal encoding.
source: Other studies have observed similar neural responses in the STN following conflict related encoding (Cavanagh et al., 2011; Zaghloul et al., 2012) and control signal encoding (Isoda and Hikosaka, 2008; Wiecki and Frank, 2013).
evidence: This is a citation to previous research findings.

claim: The task design in the present study does not allow dissection of the influence of conflict, control, and uncertainty on the observed neural responses.
source: Unfortunately, the task design in the present study does not let us dissect the influence of conflict, control, and uncertainty on the observed neural responses reported here.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the study design.

claim: The observed STN neural response may be a combination of conflict and control.
source: It is worth noting the possibility that the observed STN neural response in this experiment is a combination of conflict and control.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: A departure from a prepotent response (i.e. placing a high wager) may induce STN activity and allow for the recruitment of control centers to mediate a new decision.
source: More specifically, a departure from a prepotent response (i.e. placing a high wager) induces STN activity and allows for the recruitment of control centers to mediate a new decision.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the mechanism.

claim: The interpretation that STN activity allows recruitment of control centers would be supported by computational models and experimental data but requires further investigation.
source: This would be supported by computational models (Wiecki and Frank, 2013) and experimental data (Coulthard et al., 2012) but require further investigation to tease apart.
evidence: This is a statement about the need for further research, supported by citations.

claim: Cavanaugh et al. previously showed that increases in local-field potential oscillations in the medial prefrontal cortex and STN correlate with trial-by-trial decision conflict.
source: Furthermore, Cavanaugh et al. have previously shown that increases in local-field potential oscillations in the medial prefrontal cortex and STN correlate with trial-by-trial decision conflict and that continuous electrical stimulation through implanted DBS electrodes can prevent adjustments in decision thresholds ultimately resulting in rapid or impulsive decision-making (Cavanagh et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a citation to previous research findings.

claim: Cavanaugh et al. showed that continuous electrical stimulation through implanted DBS electrodes can prevent adjustments in decision thresholds ultimately resulting in rapid or impulsive decision-making.
source: Furthermore, Cavanaugh et al. have previously shown that increases in local-field potential oscillations in the medial prefrontal cortex and STN correlate with trial-by-trial decision conflict and that continuous electrical stimulation through implanted DBS electrodes can prevent adjustments in decision thresholds ultimately resulting in rapid or impulsive decision-making (Cavanagh et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a citation to previous research findings.

claim: The effects of stimulation may vary depending on the duration of stimulation.
source: One potential explanation for these seemingly conflicting findings is that the effects of stimulation may vary depending on the duration of stimulation.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the discrepancy between findings.

claim: Short bursts of high-frequency STN stimulation serve to increase local firing rates which are subsequently silenced with prolonged stimulation.
source: It has previously been suggested that short bursts of high-frequency STN stimulation serve to increase local firing rates which are subsequently silenced with prolonged stimulation (Lee et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a citation to previous research findings.

claim: Continuous, high-frequency stimulation has been proposed to act as an informational lesion, essentially overwriting the normal time-varying activity of the target.
source: Continuous, high-frequency stimulation has also been proposed to act as an informational lesion, essentially overwriting the normal time-varying activity of the target (Herrington et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is a citation to previous research proposing a mechanism.

claim: The finding that intermittent stimulation increases risk-averse behavior corresponds to the observed neurophysiological data where a slight increase in overall STN activity during the choice period correlates with placing a low wager.
source: Our finding also appears to correspond to the observed neurophysiological data from this study, where a slight increase in overall STN activity during the choice period correlates with placing a low wager.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the stimulation and recording findings.

claim: A limitation of the stimulation study is that stimulation was only delivered on the high-uncertainty trials, limiting the ability to understand the constraints of its effect on modifying behavior on medium- or low-uncertainty trials.
source: An interesting limitation of the stimulation study is that stimulation was only delivered on the high-uncertainty trials, limiting our ability to understand the constraints of its effect on modifying behavior on medium- or low-uncertainty trials.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the study design.

claim: The authors hypothesize the effect of stimulation would be limited or not present on low-uncertainty trials given that no differential encoding was observed.
source: We would hypothesize the effect would be limited or not present on low-uncertainty trials given that no differential encoding was observed, however this remains to be studied.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the neurophysiological findings.

claim: The current findings differ from other human neurophysiology studies in which conflict activity was observed during the stimulus presentation, as opposed to the choice period, in the dorsal anterior cingulate and the STN.
source: Interestingly, our findings differ from other human neurophysiology studies in which conflict activity was observed during the stimulus presentation, as opposed to the choice period, in the dorsal anterior cingulate (Sheth et al., 2012) and the STN (Zaghloul et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous research findings supported by citations.

claim: The intermittent stimulation technique is uniquely different than previous studies using DBS because it implements a system for rapidly turning on and off the implanted device, permitting time-locked delivery to specific task-epochs.
source: This technique is uniquely different than previous studies using DBS as a method to interrogate neural circuits because we implemented a system for rapidly turning on and off the implanted device, permitting us to time-lock delivery to specific task-epochs.
evidence: This is a description of the novel methodological approach.

claim: The intermittent stimulation approach may further reduce confounding effects of long-term stimulation, such as carry-over effects.
source: This approach may further reduce confounding effects of long-term stimulation, such as carry-over effects.
evidence: This is a speculative benefit of the methodological approach.

claim: Stimulation prior to the choice period interrupted subjects' ability to appropriately slow responses when betting against their bias (i.e. when they placed a high bet), resulting in a shortened reaction time.
source: We found that stimulation prior to the choice period interrupted subjects' ability to appropriately slow responses when betting against their bias (i.e. when they placed a high bet), resulting in a shortened reaction time, consistent with previous work (Frank et al., 2007; Cavanagh et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from the behavioral data analysis, supported by citations to previous work.

claim: There are several limitations for performing studies in the operating room, such as the length of each experimental session.
source: In the first experiment, we perform intraoperative recordings in patients undergoing a neurosurgical procedure. Naturally, there are several limitations for performing studies in the operating room, such as the length of each experimental session.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a methodological limitation.

claim: The total number of trials and neurons recorded in the intraoperative study can often be limited.
source: For this reason, the total number of trials and neurons we are able to record can often be limited.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a methodological limitation.

claim: The neurophysiological findings focus on population responses.
source: In this study, we focus our neurophysiological findings to population responses.
evidence: This is a description of the analytical approach.

claim: The reported effects are consistent across the population.
source: Despite this limitation, however, we find the reported effects to be consistent across the population.
evidence: This is a statement about the robustness of the findings.

claim: The subjects in this study all suffer from advanced PD, a disease known to affect natural reward processing.
source: Furthermore, the subjects in this study all suffer from advanced PD, a disease known to affect natural reward processing.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation related to the patient population, based on established knowledge.

claim: These experiments are constrained to populations requiring neurosurgical treatment, and direct comparisons to a healthy population are limited to behavioral measures.
source: For obvious reasons, these experiments are constrained to populations requiring neurosurgical treatment, and direct comparisons to a healthy population are limited to behavioral measures.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the study design.

claim: The study provides functional imaging and neurophysiological evidence in human subjects demonstrating the critical role of the STN in encoding decisions under conditions of uncertainty.
source: In conclusion, we provide functional imaging and neurophysiological evidence in human subjects demonstrating the critical role of the STN in encoding decisions under conditions of uncertainty.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claim: Electrical stimulation of the STN within a finite temporal window can selectively bias subject behavior towards more risk-averse decisions.
source: Moreover, we demonstrate that electrical stimulation of the STN within a finite temporal window can selectively bias subject behavior towards more risk-averse decisions.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main findings.

claim: The findings provide evidence for the role of precision neuromodulation approaches and closed-loop deep brain stimulation for the advancement of neurological and neuropsychiatric therapies.
source: Together, this provides evidence for the role of precision neuromodulation approaches and closed-loop deep brain stimulation for the advancement of neurological and neuropsychiatric therapies.
evidence: This is an inference about the broader implications of the findings.

claim: Each individual was evaluated and considered for surgery by a multidisciplinary team of neurologists, neurosurgeons, and psychiatrists.
source: Each individual was evaluated and considered for surgery by a multidisciplinary team of neurologists, neurosurgeons, and psychiatrists.
evidence: This is a description of the clinical evaluation process.

claim: All study subjects enrolled voluntarily and provided informed consent under guidelines approved by the Massachusetts General Hospital Institutional Review Board.
source: All study subjects enrolled voluntarily and provided informed consent under guidelines approved by the Massachusetts General Hospital Institutional Review Board.
evidence: This is a description of the ethical approval and consent process.

claim: The intraoperative study was approved by the Massachusetts General Hospital Institutional Review Board (protocol number 2001P000877).
source: This study was approved by the Massachusetts General Hospital Institutional Review Board (protocol number 2001P000877).
evidence: This is a statement of ethical approval.

claim: The behavioral task was presented using custom written software in Matlab, Monkey logic.
source: The behavioral task was presented using custom written software in Matlab (Math works, Natick, MA), Monkey logic (www.monkeylogic.org) (Asaad and Eskandar, 2008a; Asaad and Eskandar, 2008b; Asaad et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods with citations to the software.

claim: The task is analogous to the classic card game, War.
source: The task is analogous to the classic card game, War.
evidence: This is a description of the task design.

claim: The deck is limited to five cards: even cards from 2 through 10 from one suit.
source: To simplify the game the deck is limited to five cards: even cards from 2 through 10 from one suit.
evidence: This is a description of the task design.

claim: Each trial requires the subject to evaluate his/her card, determine its value, and place a $5 or $20 wager with the goal of maximizing profits.
source: Each trial requires the subject to evaluate his/her card, determine its value, and place a $five or $20 wager with the goal of maximizing profits.
evidence: This is a description of the task design.

claim: Each trial began with a fixation point presented at the center of the screen for 350 ms.
source: Each trial began with a fixation point presented at the center of the screen for 350 ms to indicate the start of trial (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a description of the task timing.

claim: The subject's card and the back of the opponent's card were displayed for 1000 ms.
source: Next, the subject's card and the back of the opponent's card were displayed for 1000 ms.
evidence: This is a description of the task timing.

claim: The button map was presented randomly such that the $5 and $20 wagers are assigned to the left and right buttons equally.
source: The button map was presented randomly such that the $five and $20 wagers are assigned to the left and right buttons equally.
evidence: This is a description of the task design to control for motor confounds.

claim: The time it took the subject to press a button was considered the reaction time with a maximum of 5 s.
source: The time it took the subject to press a button was considered the reaction time with a maximum of 5 s.
evidence: This is a description of the behavioral measure.

claim: Following the wager, there was a randomized delay period of 250–500 ms.
source: Following the wager, there was a randomized delay period of 250–500 ms, which was immediately followed by the presentation of the subject's and computer's card for 1000–1250 ms.
evidence: This is a description of the task timing.

claim: Feedback was given for 1000 ms by displaying an image of a $5 or $20 bill with text indicating the outcome.
source: Lastly, feedback was given for 1000 ms by displaying an image of a $five or $20 bill with text indicating the outcome.
evidence: This is a description of the task design.

claim: Subjects were monetarily rewarded following their participation in the study.
source: Subjects were monetarily rewarded following their participation in the study.
evidence: This is a description of the compensation method.

claim: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings were performed using three para-sagittal tungsten microelectrodes.
source: Intraoperative microelectrode recordings were performed using three Para-sagittal tungsten microelectrodes (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is a description of the recording methods.

claim: The electrodes were advanced using a motorized Alpha Omega Microdrive.
source: The electrodes were advanced using a motorized Alpha Omega (Alpha-Omega Engineering, Nazareth, Israel) Microdrive.
evidence: This is a description of the recording equipment.

claim: Recordings were band-pass filtered between 300 Hz and 6.5 kHz by an Alpha Omega acquisition system.
source: Recordings were band-pass filtered between 300 Hz and 6.5 kHz by an Alpha Omega acquisition system.
evidence: This is a description of the signal processing methods.

claim: Data was recorded at 20 kHz by a PowerLinc 1401 acquisition system.
source: Data was recorded at 20 kHz by a PowerLinc 1401 acquisition system (Cambridge Electronic Design, Cambridge, England) and stored for post-hoc analysis.
evidence: This is a description of the data acquisition methods.

claim: The neurophysiology data was sorted into individual neuronal records using a template clustering method (Offline Sorter, Plexon).
source: Offline, the neurophysiology data was sorted into individual neuronal records using a template clustering method (Offline Sorter, Plexon, Houston, TX).
evidence: This is a description of the spike sorting methods.

claim: All analyses were performed using a combination of iPython and R.
source: All analyses were performed using a combination of iPython and R.
evidence: This is a description of the analysis software.

claim: Reaction time data was z-scored using each session's mean and variance reaction time to account for inter-subject variability in baseline motor performance.
source: Because of inter-subject variability in baseline motor performance, we explored reaction time differences by first z-scoring data using each session's mean and variance reaction time.
evidence: This is a description of the data normalization method.

claim: The instantaneous firing rate was approximated by convolving a Gaussian kernel (sigma = 150 ms) with 1 ms binned spike trains.
source: To visualize neural activity, the instantaneous firing rate was approximated by convolving a Gaussian kernel (sigma = 150 ms) with 1 ms binned spike trains.
evidence: This is a description of the neural data processing method.

claim: Statistical analyses at the individual cell level were rarely significant due to limitations in the number of trials recorded in each experimental session.
source: Because of the limitations in the number of trials recorded in each experimental session, statistical analyses at the individual cell level were rarely significant, and instead all analyses were performed at the population level.
evidence: This is an explanation of the analytical approach based on data limitations.

claim: Coefficients in the regression model were estimated through a least-squares approach.
source: Coefficients were estimated through a least-squares approach.
evidence: This is a description of the parameter estimation method.

claim: The intermittent stimulation study was approved by the Massachusetts General Hospital Institutional Review Board (protocol number 2007P001806).
source: This study was approved by the Massachusetts General Hospital Institutional Review Board (protocol number 2007P001806).
evidence: This is a statement of ethical approval.

claim: On the day of the intermittent stimulation study, the patient's deep brain stimulator was turned off after obtaining written informed consent.
source: On the day of the study, after obtaining written informed consent, the patient's deep brain stimulator was turned off.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol.

claim: The stimulation voltage was lowered in small increments with the stimulator being turned on and off in a blinded fashion until a voltage threshold was reached at which the patient was unable to detect the stimulation.
source: Subsequently the stimulation voltage was lowered in small increments with the stimulator being turned on and off in a blinded fashion until a voltage threshold was reached at which the patient was unable to detect the stimulation.
evidence: This is a description of the blinding procedure.

claim: After approximately 15 min with the stimulator off, the patient began playing the task.
source: The stimulator controller was secured over the patient's pulse generator, and after approximately 15 min with the stimulator off, the patient began playing the task.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol.

claim: Three different stimulation conditions were used on 6-card trials: 1 s of stimulation at the fixation epoch, 1 s of stimulation at the choice period, or no stimulation was delivered.
source: We used three different stimulation conditions on 6-card trials: 1 s of stimulation at the fixation epoch, 1 s of stimulation at the choice period, or no stimulation was delivered.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design.

claim: The design allowed each subject to act as his own control, helping to account for variance due to differing disease, medication, and electrode location factors between patients.
source: This design allowed each subject to act as his own control, helping to account for variance due to differing disease, medication, and electrode location factors between patients and also allowed us to control for general versus time specific effects of stimulation.
evidence: This is an explanation of the rationale for the within-subjects design.
